title: LoggedModel.to_proto must write every field that from_proto reads (status_message was dropped)
answers: logged model status message lost after proto round trip
FAILED logged model reason missing when fetched via REST or proto
body:
Symptom: A logged model that FAILED with a reason shows no failure message once it has gone through its proto form (status_message comes back empty).
Root cause: mlflow/entities/logged_model.py:LoggedModel.to_proto never set status_message on pb2.LoggedModelInfo, while LoggedModel.from_proto reads it.
Fix pattern: Set the missing field in to_proto alongside the other info fields (status_message=self.status_message), so the serializer and the parser stay symmetric.
Constraints: When adding or changing any LoggedModel field, update both to_proto and from_proto. A proto round-trip test (to_proto then from_proto, assert equality) catches a field that is read but never written; see tests/entities/test_logged_model.py:test_logged_model_proto_round_trip_keeps_status_message.
applies: Applies to changes to LoggedModel fields or its proto (de)serialization in mlflow/entities/logged_model.py.
says: A failed logged model shows an empty failure reason when viewed.
The error message is missing on models that have a failed status.
Show the failure reason when inspecting a logged model that failed.
Details pane for a failed model does not display the explanation message.
search: LoggedModel.to_proto in mlflow/entities/logged_model.py must write every field read by LoggedModel.from_proto, including status_message on pb2.LoggedModelInfo. Omitting status_message in to_proto causes models in a FAILED state to lose their failure message upon proto deserialization. Any changes to LoggedModel fields require updating both serialization and deserialization symmetrically. Symmetric round-trip behavior is verified in tests/entities/test_logged_model.py:test_logged_model_proto_round_trip_keeps_status_message by asserting equality across to_proto and from_proto conversions.
